title: Alien Dictionary
kidExplanation: Alien words in sorted order. Recover the alphabet order (topological sort) if possible.
plainProblem: Alien Dictionary: Alien words in sorted order. Worked example — input: words = ["wrt","wrf","er","ett","rftt"]; expected output: "wertf". Why: Order. Interview pattern to name out loud: Dijkstra / topological sort.

thinkingSteps.title: Brute force idea
thinkingSteps.body: For “Alien Dictionary”, first say a correct slow approach: scan or retry every candidate until the example works by hand. Input words = ["wrt","wrf","er","ett","rftt"] should still produce "wertf".

thinkingSteps.title: Why it is slow
thinkingSteps.body: Count the nested work. If each choice restarts a full scan, time blows up. Name the cost before optimizing — interviewers want that honesty. Target after the insight: See code.

thinkingSteps.title: Aha insight
thinkingSteps.body: The problem can be solved using topological sorting. The given words can be thought of as directed edges between characters of adjacent words. We can build a graph where each character is a node, and the edges represent the order between characters. Then, we can perform topological sorting to find the correct order of characters.
